subject: Career
title: Halo Effect in Hiring
description: A micro-lesson that makes Halo Effect in Hiring usable.

hook.text: A candidate from Google applies. The recruiter assumes they're brilliant before reading a word.

buildup.text: The halo effect means one positive trait makes us assume other positive traits exist.

discovery.text: Brand-name companies, elite schools, and prestigious titles create halos on resumes.

twist.text: If you don't have a halo, you need proof. Measurable results beat brand names.

climax.text: 'Grew revenue 40%' outperforms 'worked at unknown company' every time.

punchline.text: No famous brand? Let your results be famous.

quiz.question: What is the halo effect in hiring?
options: One positive trait makes us assume other positives

details.summary: The halo effect in hiring causes one impressive credential, like a prestigious employer or university, to positively bias the evaluation of your entire resume. Strategic placement of your strongest credential creates a favorable lens through which everything else is viewed.
details.whyItMatters: A single prominent credential can carry more influence than the rest of your resume combined. Knowing where to place it and how to leverage it maximizes its halo potential.
takeaways: Place your most impressive credential where it will be seen first
Prestigious employers and universities create strong positive halos
Be aware that halo effects can work against you with misperceived credentials

faq.question: How can you create a halo effect on your resume without prestigious credentials?
faq.answer: Major quantified accomplishments, recognizable client names, industry awards, and impressive project scale all create halos. Leading with 'Increased revenue by two million dollars' has halo power regardless of the employer's name. Impact metrics can substitute for institutional prestige.

faq.question: Can the halo effect from a prestigious employer backfire in certain hiring contexts?
faq.answer: Yes. Some startups or small companies may view big-company backgrounds with suspicion, assuming you are too corporate or slow-moving. In these cases, emphasize scrappy accomplishments and entrepreneurial behaviors to counter the potential negative halo of a bureaucratic reputation.
